hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are grumbling about Adidas' kit designs again — 'last year's effort' clearly left a bad taste — while a cryptic Spanish post hints at legal/judicial frustrations ('cositas de jueces'). The women's team conceding to Graham Hansen, with Barcelona unbeaten in 28 UWCL games when she scores, adds salt to the wound. Not a crisis, but the grumbles are audible from the Emirates.

daily.summary: The day began with ambitious transfer optimism and quiet confidence, dipped midday into a swaggering but cynical bullishness tinged with concerns over club priorities and player fitness, then finished on a high note of resilient pride after the women's team held Barcelona and the men's side earned recognition as the country's best. The arc moves from hopeful dreaming to justified, grounded confidence.

weekly.summary: The week began in euphoric triumph after a historic Anfield victory that sent Arsenal top, but sentiment quickly volatilized — swinging from confident title-race dominance to transfer-market cynicism and squad-management anxiety by mid-week. A recovery followed as rivals faltered and Arsenal extended their lead to six points, yet the prevailing mood remained edgy: fans frame every win as survival, haunted by refereeing paranoia, injury fears, and a siege mentality that refuses comfort even in success.
